Message: VACUUM EQUIPMENT GROUPS (groupName)
Every VacuumPumps item has a groupName. Items sharing a groupName form one cascade stage:
they are energized together, and every member must be ready before the next stage starts.
Stages run in the order their groupName first appears. If a stage loses readiness,
every stage downstream of it is switched off. MechanicalVacuumPump is never switched off.
MechanicalVacuum  -> MechanicalVacuumPump (backing stage, always on)
TurboVacuum       -> TurboVacuumPump, TurboVacuumPump_2
UltraHighVacuum   -> UHVacuumPump_1, UHVacuumPump_2, UHVacuumPump_3, UHVacuumPump_4
A pump turns ready (green) only when its ready input is on and, when a gauge reading is
available, the reading exactly matches the configured value or is lower.
Rules:
- groupName starts with a letter and uses only letters, digits, '_' or '-'.
- The first groupName contains only MechanicalVacuumPump.
- At least two groupName stages are required.
- List the items of one groupName next to each other.
SBC GPIO MAPPING (Raspberry Pi naming)
A0..A7 and B0..B7 are logical application channel names.
SBC.GPIO.<logical channel> is the Raspberry Pi GPIO line name GPIOn, as printed by pinout, gpioinfo and pinctrl.
GPIOn is the Broadcom (BCM) line number, not the physical header pin number.
Logical channel                 Purpose
A0..A7                         Equipment or high-voltage transformer output
B0..B7                         Comparator/status input

An alternate-function line may be used as plain GPIO only when that interface and its device-tree overlay are disabled.
GPIO18 (PCM CLK/PWM0) and GPIO19 (PCM FS/PWM1/SPI1 MISO) are assigned to A7/B7; disable conflicting interfaces and overlays.
CHANGING THE EQUIPMENT COUNT
- The equipment list is configuration-driven: 3 to 8 VacuumPumps items.
- Every item needs a groupName, one unused logical A output and one unused logical B input.
- Add both logical channels to SBC.GPIO, each with an unused GPIOn line.
- Equipment names, write channels, read channels and GPIO lines must be unique.
ELECTRICAL SAFETY
- Raspberry Pi GPIO uses 3.3 V logic and is not 5 V tolerant.
- Never connect pumps, contactors, solenoids or relay coils directly to GPIO.
- Use galvanically isolated, appropriately rated input/output interface circuitry.
- Provide hardware-defined safe output states during boot, shutdown and SBC power loss.
COMMISSIONING WARNING
The committed SBC.GPIO lines are initial assignments only.
Verify every GPIOn-to-header-pin connection with pinout on the final Raspberry Pi, the carrier schematic,
the relay interface and the wiring drawing before changing Simulate to false.
